subject: Key access model + network segmentation for private deploy — review and action items
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Chris Yang <chris.yang@acme.com>
Cc: ACME SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Key access model + network segmentation for private deploy — review and action items

Team / Chris —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. Per ACME's request we put together a first-pass Key Access Model and a concise network-zone diagram for the private VPC deployment. Attached: key-entitlement-matrix-v1.xlsx and network-zone-diagram.pdf.

High-level asks from ACME:
- BYOK retention requirements (they want on-prem HSM custody, but desire operator separation)
- Minimal egress for any unseal or key retrieval flows
- Clear emergency rotation runbook and audit evidence they can surface to auditors

What I need from the team for Friday's internal readiness review:
1) Monica — confirm the entitlement matrix columns: who can request key material, who can perform remote unseal, who has emergency revoke ability. Please mark any service accounts we should add.
2) Dylan — validate the network flows on page 2 of the diagram: dedicated management plane vs workload plane, and explicit ports for HSM/PKCS#11, KMIP, and control-plane pull.
3) Laura — compile minimal SOC2 evidence we can give ACME pre-onboarding (retention policy, access logs snippet, KMS integration test results). I attached a zip placeholder partial-soc2-evidence.zip for the items we already have documented.

Notes / constraints:
- We should not rely on outbound internet for unseal or key material transfer; any egress should be via controlled jump-hosts with egress-only peering and strict ACLs.
- Prefer HSM with support for remote attestation and split custody quorum (n of m) so ACME can maintain key ownership.
- Plan to expose an operator-facing bastion in a separate management VPC with explicit routing to the HSM subnet; application traffic must never have direct access to operator bastion.

Chris — please flag anything we missed or incorrect in the attached before EOD tomorrow and note any ACME constraints we should bake in.

Thanks,

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- key-entitlement-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- network-zone-diagram.pdf (diagram)
- partial-soc2-evidence.zip (zip)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Yang <chris.yang@acme.com>, ACME SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key access model + network segmentation for private deploy — review and action items

Thanks Rishi — quick pass notes after reviewing key-entitlement-matrix-v1.xlsx:

- I added a Service Account row for the "deploy-agent" we use in Dedicated installations; it needs "request-key" but not "remote-unseal".
- Suggested renames: Operator -> "Key Custody Operator" (makes the audit logs clearer), Break-Glass -> "Emergency Escrow Custodian".
- For emergency revoke we should require 2FA + a quorum of 2 human operators + HSM module approval; added a column to the sheet indicating quorum size.
- Flag: the matrix currently lists "remote-unseal via API" — we should make that "remote-unseal via HSM-attested session" and require mutual TLS from the management bastion.

Action items I propose before the internal review:
- I'll update the spreadsheet with the service account and quorum column (done).
- Dylan to confirm the IP ranges and the port list so I can reference them in the matrix.
- Laura to attach the access-log sample (sanitized) to the SOC2 evidence zip.

On the network diagram: recommend we show an explicit jump-host NAT that performs signed, audited unseal requests to the HSM and logs request IDs back to our control-plane. This reduces direct egress from the HSM zone.

Monica
Lead Security PM, Redwood Inference

From: Chris Yang <chris.yang@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME SecOps <secops@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key access model + network segmentation for private deploy — review and action items

Rishi / Monica / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from ACME SecOps perspective: 

1) BYOK custody: ACME wants hardware-backed keys retained within our HSM; we will retain master key shares in our safes. We still want Redwood to run the unseal orchestration but only after ACME operators initiate the quorum from their side (so split approval).
2) Egress: acceptable if the jump-host has an authorized egress to our corporate colocation via IPsec to a fixed peer and every unseal request must be logged both by Redwood and by ACME (mutual logging).
3) API vs HSM: remote-unseal must be via an attested HSM channel (no plaintext key material over API). We can support a KMIP tunnel from the HSM to Redwood control plane for HA replication, provided it is initiated by ACME.

Questions:
- Does Redwood support an operator separation model where ACME's human operators trigger quorum acceptance from within their environment and Redwood only orchestrates the signed challenge? If not, we need to document the exact containment boundaries.
- In the case of emergency rotation, can staff perform an offline key rotation procedure with a sealed material import into the HSM, or is rotation always online?

We'll review the updated matrix once Monica publishes the new columns. We can provision a temporary test HSM instance on our side for a rehearsal next week. Let us know available windows.

— Chris Yang
Head of SecOps, ACME Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Chris Yang <chris.yang@acme.com>
Cc: ACME SecOps <secops@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Key access model + network segmentation for private deploy — review and action items

Thanks Chris — good questions. Short answers and next steps: 

- Operator separation model: yes — we support a flow where ACME operators trigger a locally-held quorum; Redwood's orchestration only relays signed challenge tokens and runs the sequencer. I'll attach a sequence diagram to the drive link; we will not hold plaintext master material in our control plane.
- Emergency rotation: we support both online rotation (HSM-to-HSM key rewrap with versioned rollouts) and an offline sealed-import path. The offline path requires importable wrapped keys that the HSM will unseal locally under ACME control — documented in the runbook draft.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Monica: publish final entitlement matrix and mark any service-account exceptions (due Fri 19 Mar EOD).
- Dylan: confirm IP ranges/ports and produce an ACL snippet for the management VPC (due Fri 19 Mar COB).
- Laura: attach sanitized access-log and the retention policy excerpt into partial-soc2-evidence.zip and share Drive link (due Mon 22 Mar).
- Chris/ACME: available for a 60m rehearsal next Wed 24 Mar? They suggested provisioning a test HSM.

I'll prepare a short canary script that exercises the signed-challenge flow for the rehearsal. If we can run a timed rehearsal, we should capture the request IDs on both sides to validate mutual logging.

Rishi
Sr. Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
